question: Which Delhi sultan was known for his "Market Reforms"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alauddin Khalji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alauddin Khalji (of the Khalji dynasty) is famous for his Market Reforms (बाज़ार सुधार), introduced mainly to maintain a large standing army at low cost.

• He fixed the prices of essential commodities and set up separate markets for grain, cloth, horses and slaves.

• Officers like the Shahna-i-Mandi (market controller) and Diwan-i-Riyasat enforced strict price control.

• He also introduced measures to check hoarding and black-marketing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Alauddin Khalji ruled from 1296 to 1316 AD and was the most powerful ruler of the Khalji dynasty.

• He was the first Sultan to introduce a permanent standing army paid in cash.

• His general Malik Kafur led successful expeditions into South India.

NOTE

• Balban (Option 1): A powerful ruler of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty known for the theory of kingship and 'Sijda' and 'Paibos'.

• Firoz Shah Tughlaq (Option 2): Tughlaq ruler known for public works, canals and imposition of Jizya on Brahmins.

• Iltutmish (Option 4): Slave dynasty ruler who introduced the silver 'tanka' and copper 'jital' coins.

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Canada?
option_1: Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme court
solution_text:
The correct answer is Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (उच्चतम न्यायालय का सलाहकार क्षेत्राधिकार) is borrowed from the Constitution of Canada.

• Other features borrowed from Canada include a strong Centre (federation with a strong centre), residuary powers with the Centre, and appointment of state Governors by the Centre.

• Article 143 empowers the President to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• From the USA India borrowed Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review and impeachment of the President.

• From Ireland came Directive Principles and the method of election of the President.

• From the UK came Parliamentary government, Rule of Law and single citizenship.

NOTE

• Rule of Law (Option 2): Borrowed from the British Constitution (UK).

• Impeachment of the President (Option 3): Borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.

• Fundamental duties (Option 4): Inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

question: Which of the following is not covered under Article 25 of the Indian Constitution?
option_2: Right to profess and practice religion
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to religious conversion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 25 guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practise and propagate religion (धर्म को मानने, आचरण और प्रचार की स्वतंत्रता).

• It does not grant a Right to religious conversion; the word 'propagate' does not include a right to convert another person.

• The right is subject to public order, morality and health.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 25 is part of the Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28).

• Article 26 deals with freedom to manage religious affairs.

• Article 27 prohibits taxes for promotion of a religion, and Article 28 deals with religious instruction in educational institutions.

NOTE

• Freedom of Conscience (Option 1): Expressly guaranteed under Article 25.

• Right to profess and practice religion (Option 2): Expressly covered under Article 25.

• Right to propagate religion (Option 3): Expressly covered under Article 25.

question: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank is headquartered in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beijing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (एशियाई अवसंरचना निवेश बैंक) is headquartered in Beijing, China.

• The AIIB was established in 2016 and is a multilateral development bank focused on infrastructure in Asia and beyond.

• India is one of the founding members and is the second-largest shareholder after China.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first President of AIIB was Jin Liqun.

• AIIB was proposed by China in 2013 and formally launched in January 2016.

• Its aim is to support sustainable infrastructure and connectivity projects.

NOTE

• Shanghai (Option 2): The financial hub of China and headquarters of the New Development Bank (BRICS Bank), not AIIB.

• New Delhi (Option 3): The capital of India; not the AIIB headquarters.

• Bangkok (Option 4): The capital of Thailand and headquarters of UNESCAP, not AIIB.

question: Agreement on cooperation in the peaceful uses of Nuclear energy was signed in _____ between India and Japan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The India–Japan Agreement for Cooperation in the Peaceful Uses of Nuclear Energy (परमाणु ऊर्जा के शांतिपूर्ण उपयोग पर समझौता) was signed in 2016.

• It was signed during the visit of PM Narendra Modi to Japan in November 2016.

• This made Japan the first country with which India signed such a civil nuclear pact despite being a non-signatory of the NPT.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The agreement enabled the transfer of nuclear technology, material and reactors for civilian use.

• The deal came into force in 2017.

• Japan's cooperation was significant for India's civil nuclear programme after the 2008 NSG waiver.

NOTE

• 2008 (Option 1): The year of the India–US civil nuclear deal (123 Agreement) and NSG waiver, not the India–Japan pact.

• 2012 (Option 2): Not the year of signing of the India–Japan nuclear agreement.

• 2020 (Option 4): Not the year of signing of the India–Japan nuclear agreement.

question: Hariprasad Chaurasia is a celebrated classical musician known for playing which instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a world-renowned Indian classical musician famous for playing the Flute (बांसुरी) — specifically the Bansuri.

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2000.

• He popularised the bansuri in Hindustani classical music at a global level.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He also composed music (with Shivkumar Sharma) under the name Shiv-Hari for Hindi films.

• He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and many international honours.

• The bansuri is a side-blown bamboo flute associated with Lord Krishna.

NOTE

• Sitar (Option 1): A plucked string instrument mastered by Pandit Ravi Shankar.

• Violin (Option 3): A bowed string instrument; noted Indian exponents include L. Subramaniam.

• Tabla (Option 4): A pair of percussion drums; Zakir Hussain is a famous tabla maestro.

question: Which ministry has launched 'Deen Dayal SPARSH Yojana' in August 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Communications.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Deen Dayal SPARSH Yojana (दीन दयाल स्पर्श योजना) is a scholarship scheme launched by the Department of Posts under the Ministry of Communications (संचार मंत्रालय).

• SPARSH stands for Scholarship for Promotion of Aptitude & Research in Stamps as a Hobby.

• It promotes Philately (stamp collection) among school children in classes VI to IX.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme provides an annual scholarship to meritorious students with a keen interest in philately.

• The Department of Posts functions under the Ministry of Communications.

• India Post issues commemorative stamps and runs philately promotion activities.

NOTE

• Ministry of Agriculture (Option 1): Handles farming, crops and rural agrarian schemes, not philately.

• Ministry of Power (Option 3): Deals with electricity generation and distribution.

• Ministry of Defence (Option 4): Handles the armed forces and national defence.

question: Who publishes the Global Terrorism Index 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Institute for Economics and Peace.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Global Terrorism Index (वैश्विक आतंकवाद सूचकांक) is published by the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP), an Australia-based think tank.

• The index ranks countries based on the impact of terrorism.

• It uses data from sources including the Terrorism Tracker.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The IEP also publishes the Global Peace Index and the Positive Peace Index.

• The GTI measures deaths, incidents, hostages and injuries from terrorism.

• It was founded by Steve Killelea.

NOTE

• SIPRI (Option 1): Stockholm International Peace Research Institute; publishes data on arms, military spending and disarmament.

• United Nations (Option 3): Global intergovernmental body; does not publish the GTI.

• WHO (Option 4): World Health Organization; deals with global public health.

question: Which organization publishes the Human Development Report?
solution_text:
The correct answer is UNDP.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Human Development Report (मानव विकास रिपोर्ट) is published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

• It introduced the Human Development Index (HDI) in 1990, based on life expectancy, education and per capita income.

• The concept was developed by economists Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• UNDP is headquartered in New York, USA.

• The HDI classifies countries into very high, high, medium and low human development.

• The report also includes indices like the Gender Inequality Index and Multidimensional Poverty Index.

NOTE

• IMF (Option 2): Publishes the World Economic Outlook and manages global monetary cooperation.

• World Bank (Option 3): Publishes reports like the World Development Report and Ease of Doing Business (earlier).

• World Economic Forum (Option 4): Publishes the Global Competitiveness Report and Global Gender Gap Report.

question: State Health Index is an initiative of NITI Aayog, in collaboration with Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and with technical assistance from the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The State Health Index (राज्य स्वास्थ्य सूचकांक) is an initiative of NITI Aayog in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and with technical assistance from the World Bank (विश्व बैंक).

• It is an annual tool to measure and compare the overall performance and incremental improvement of states and UTs in health outcomes.

• The report is titled 'Healthy States, Progressive India'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The index groups states into 'Larger States', 'Smaller States' and 'Union Territories'.

• It uses indicators grouped under domains of Health Outcomes, Governance and Key Inputs/Processes.

• NITI Aayog was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

NOTE

• Institute for Competitiveness (Option 1): A think tank that partners on indices like the Export Preparedness Index, not the technical partner here.

• CSIR (Option 2): Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, a science research body.

• Ministry of Earth Sciences (Option 4): Handles weather, climate and ocean sciences, not the State Health Index.

question: Steeplechase is a hurdle race with water jumps came into existence in England around _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1850.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Steeplechase (स्टीपलचेज़) is a distance running race on a track with hurdles and water jumps (barriers).

• As a track event it came into existence in England around 1850.

• The name originally comes from horse races run towards a church steeple as a landmark.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The standard Olympic steeplechase is the 3000 metres steeplechase.

• The race includes 28 barrier jumps and 7 water jumps.

• It became a regular men's Olympic event and later a women's event (from 2008).

NOTE

• 1900 (Option 2): The year steeplechase was introduced in the modern Olympic Games (Paris), not when the race originated.

• 1710 (Option 3): Too early; not the accepted date for the athletics steeplechase in England.

• 1980 (Option 4): Not associated with the origin of the steeplechase.

question: The Farakka barrage is situated on _____ river.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ganga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Farakka Barrage (फरक्का बैराज) is situated on the Ganga (Ganges) river in West Bengal.

• It was built to divert water into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly river to flush out silt from the Kolkata port.

• It became operational in 1975.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The barrage is a subject of the India–Bangladesh Ganga Water Sharing Treaty (1996).

• It is located near the town of Farakka in Murshidabad district.

• A feeder canal carries water from the barrage to the Bhagirathi.

NOTE

• Mahanadi (Option 2): A river in Odisha/Chhattisgarh; the Hirakud Dam is built on it.

• Godavari (Option 3): The largest peninsular river, often called the 'Dakshin Ganga'.

• Luni (Option 4): A river of Rajasthan that ends in the Rann of Kutch.

question: Which city will host the 2032 Summer Olympics Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brisbane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Brisbane (ब्रिस्बेन), in Australia, will host the 2032 Summer Olympic Games.

• It was awarded the Games by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 2021.

• This will be the third Summer Olympics held in Australia, after Melbourne (1956) and Sydney (2000).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France.

• The 2028 Summer Olympics will be held in Los Angeles, USA.

• The IOC is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

NOTE

• Doha (Option 2): Capital of Qatar; hosted the 2019 World Athletics Championships and 2022 FIFA World Cup.

• Salt Lake City (Option 3): A US city set to host the 2034 Winter Olympics.

• Nice (Option 4): A city in France; not an awarded Summer Olympics host.

question:
Which of the following is a purpose of remote sensing satellites?
I. Draught assessment
II. Estimation of yield of various crops
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Remote sensing satellites (सुदूर संवेदन उपग्रह) are used for both drought assessment and estimation of crop yield.

• They capture data about the Earth's surface using electromagnetic radiation without physical contact.

• Both statements I and II are valid applications, so the answer is Both I and II.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Remote sensing is also used in land use mapping, forestry, mineral exploration and disaster management.

• India's remote sensing satellites include the IRS series and Resourcesat, Cartosat satellites.

• The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) is under ISRO.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, as crop yield estimation (statement II) is also a valid purpose.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, as drought assessment (statement I) is also a valid purpose.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are correct applications.

question: The 'Mangalyaan' mission of India was launched by, which of the following launch vehicle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PSLV.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's Mangalyaan (मंगलयान) — the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM) — was launched by the PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle), PSLV-C25.

• It was launched on 5 November 2013 and entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.

• India became the first nation to reach Mars orbit in its first attempt.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The mission was executed by ISRO at a very low cost (~₹450 crore).

• India was the first Asian country to reach Mars orbit.

• The PSLV is called ISRO's 'workhorse' launch vehicle.

NOTE

• SLV-3 (Option 1): India's first experimental Satellite Launch Vehicle, which launched Rohini in 1980.

• ASLV (Option 2): Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle, an experimental launcher of the 1980s–90s.

• GSLV (Option 4): Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, used for heavier communication satellites and Chandrayaan-2.

question: The "Chandrayaan-2" mission was launched by, which of the following launching vehicle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is GSLV.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chandrayaan-2 (चंद्रयान-2) was launched by the GSLV Mk III (GSLV-Mk III-M1) launch vehicle.

• It was launched on 22 July 2019 from Sriharikota.

• It comprised an Orbiter, a Lander (Vikram) and a Rover (Pragyan).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• GSLV Mk III (now LVM3) is India's heaviest launch vehicle.

• The Chandrayaan-2 orbiter is still functional around the Moon.

• Chandrayaan-3 later achieved a successful soft landing near the lunar south pole in 2023.

NOTE

• SLV-3 (Option 1): India's first experimental Satellite Launch Vehicle (1980).

• ASLV (Option 2): Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle, an experimental launcher.

• PSLV (Option 4): Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, used for Chandrayaan-1 and Mangalyaan.

question: Which institute has developed hybrid aerogel to extract gold from e-waste in December 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IISER, Pune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Researchers at IISER Pune (आई.आई.एस.ई.आर., पुणे) developed a hybrid aerogel to extract gold from electronic waste (ई-कचरे से सोना) in December 2024.

• The hybrid aerogel is a lightweight, highly porous material that selectively captures gold ions from e-waste.

• The work supports eco-friendly recovery of precious metals and reduces electronic pollution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• IISER (Indian Institute of Science Education and Research) institutes focus on science education and research.

• The research was published in a leading international chemistry journal.

• E-waste recycling helps recover valuable metals like gold, silver and copper.

NOTE

• IISER, Tirupati (Option 1): An IISER campus in Andhra Pradesh; not credited with this aerogel work.

• IISER, Mohali (Option 2): An IISER campus in Punjab; not the developing institute here.

• IISER, Bhopal (Option 4): An IISER campus in Madhya Pradesh; not the developing institute here.

question: Which space agency has launched the PUNCH Mission in March 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NASA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The PUNCH Mission (पंच मिशन) was launched by NASA (नासा) in March 2025.

• PUNCH stands for Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere.

• It studies how the Sun's corona becomes the solar wind, using four small satellites.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PUNCH was launched along with the SPHEREx observatory on a single rocket.

• The mission helps understand space weather that affects Earth.

• NASA is the space agency of the United States, headquartered in Washington, D.C.

NOTE

• ESA (Option 1): European Space Agency; did not launch the PUNCH mission.

• JAXA (Option 3): Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency; not associated with PUNCH.

• ISRO (Option 4): Indian Space Research Organisation; its solar mission is Aditya-L1, not PUNCH.

question: Which of the following factors determine the state of a substance whether it will be solid, liquid or gas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pressure and temperature.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The physical state of a substance (पदार्थ की अवस्था) — solid, liquid or gas — is determined by Pressure and Temperature (दाब और तापमान).

• Increasing temperature generally converts solids to liquids to gases (as inter-particle forces weaken).

• Increasing pressure tends to bring particles closer, favouring the liquid or solid state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas (plasma being the fourth).

• Change of state occurs at fixed temperatures like melting point and boiling point.

• Processes include melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation and sublimation.

NOTE

• Density and viscosity (Option 2): These are properties of matter, not the deciding factors of its state.

• Pressure and density (Option 3): Density is a property that results from state, not a primary determining factor.

• Temperature and weight (Option 4): Weight does not determine the physical state of a substance.

question: How many astronomical observatories were constructed by Sawai Jai Singh, the ruler of Amber?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sawai Jai Singh II, the ruler of Amber (Jaipur), constructed five astronomical observatories (पांच वेधशालाएं) known as Jantar Mantar.

• These were built at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura and Varanasi.

• They were built in the early 18th century to make accurate astronomical observations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Jaipur Jantar Mantar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• It houses the world's largest stone sundial, the Samrat Yantra.

• Jai Singh II founded the city of Jaipur in 1727.

NOTE

• Nine (Option 2): Incorrect count; Jai Singh built five observatories.

• Ten (Option 3): Incorrect count of the Jantar Mantar observatories.

• Twelve (Option 4): Incorrect count of the Jantar Mantar observatories.

question: What tragic incident happened in the life of Robert Clive in 1774?
option_4: He was given death penalty on the charges of corruption.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He committed suicide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Robert Clive, the first British Governor of Bengal, committed suicide (आत्महत्या) in 1774.

• He is credited with laying the foundation of British rule in India after the Battle of Plassey (1757) and Battle of Buxar (1764).

• He faced a parliamentary inquiry over corruption charges before his death.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Clive introduced the Dual System of Government in Bengal in 1765.

• He obtained the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha from the Mughal emperor.

• He served as Governor of Bengal in two terms.

NOTE

• He was assassinated (Option 1): Incorrect; Clive was not killed by an assassin.

• He was exiled to Burma (Option 3): Incorrect; this fate is associated with the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar.

• He was given death penalty on the charges of corruption (Option 4): Incorrect; he was censured but not executed.

question: In the context of the Indian Parliament, the _____ Reading refers to the discussion on the motion that the Bill or the Bill, as amended, be passed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Third.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Indian Parliament's legislative process, the Third Reading (तीसरा वाचन) refers to the discussion on the motion that the Bill (or the Bill as amended) be passed.

• At this stage the debate is limited to accepting or rejecting the Bill, with no further amendments to details.

• A Bill is deemed passed by a House after the Third Reading.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The First Reading is the introduction of the Bill.

• The Second Reading involves detailed and clause-by-clause consideration.

• After passing in both Houses, the Bill goes to the President for assent (Article 111).

NOTE

• First (Option 1): The stage at which the Bill is introduced and its title read out.

• Second (Option 2): The stage of general discussion and clause-by-clause scrutiny of the Bill.

• Fourth (Option 4): There is no fourth reading in the standard legislative procedure.

question: Which of the following enzyme is secreted by the pancreas for digesting emulsified fats in humans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lipase.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pancreatic Lipase (लाइपेज़) is the enzyme secreted by the pancreas to digest emulsified fats (इमल्सीकृत वसा) in humans.

• It breaks down fats (triglycerides) into fatty acids and glycerol.

• Bile (from the liver) first emulsifies fats so that lipase can act on them efficiently.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The pancreas is both an exocrine and endocrine gland.

• Pancreatic juice also contains amylase and proteases (trypsin, chymotrypsin).

• Fat digestion mainly occurs in the small intestine.

NOTE

• Amylase (Option 1): Digests carbohydrates (starch) into sugars; present in saliva and pancreatic juice.

• Trypsin (Option 3): A pancreatic protease that digests proteins into peptides, not fats.

• Lactase (Option 4): An intestinal enzyme that digests lactose (milk sugar), not fats.

question:
Which of the following waste product in stored in old xylem of plants?
I. Resins
II. Gums
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In plants, waste products such as Resins and Gums (रेजिन और गोंद) are stored in the old xylem (heartwood).

• As xylem ages, it stops conducting water and gets filled with such organic waste materials.

• Hence both statements I (Resins) and II (Gums) are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Plants store waste in various forms as they lack a proper excretory system.

• Other plant waste products include tannins, latex, alkaloids and essential oils.

• Some wastes like raphides (calcium oxalate) are stored in leaves and stems.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, as gums (statement II) are also stored in old xylem.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, as resins (statement I) are also stored in old xylem.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both resins and gums are stored there.

question: In the context of the Sangam age of South India, the term 'Sangam' refers to _____.
option_1: a royal festival of Tamil kings
option_3: a gathering of South Indian traders
option_4: an assembly or 'meeting together' of Tamil poets
solution_text:
The correct answer is an assembly or 'meeting together' of Tamil poets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Sangam Age (संगम युग) of South India, the term 'Sangam' refers to an assembly or 'meeting together' of Tamil poets (तमिल कवियों का समागम).

• These assemblies of poets and scholars were held under royal patronage, especially of the Pandya kings of Madurai.

• The literature produced is known as Sangam literature.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Tradition mentions three Sangams (Muchchangam).

• Major Sangam works include Tolkappiyam, and the epics Silappadikaram and Manimekalai.

• The Sangam Age was dominated by the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas.

NOTE

• a royal festival of Tamil kings (Option 1): Incorrect; Sangam was a scholarly assembly, not a festival.

• a council of military leaders (Option 2): Incorrect; it was an academy of poets, not a military body.

• a gathering of South Indian traders (Option 3): Incorrect; it referred to poets and scholars, not traders.
